info.bio: Rod Stewart, músico británico, nació el 10 de enero del año 1945 en Highgate (Londres). Comenzó su carrera en la banda de Brian Auger (The Brian Augen Trinity), pasó por los Steampackets, y alcanzó la fama en la banda de Jeff Beck y en los Faces (Junto a Ron Wood, de Rolling Stones). En su carrera en solitario era una estrella de rock al comienzo, pero finalmente ha tomado un tono baladístico que lo ha alejado de las nuevas generaciones.

scenes.name: El disco
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: Una simulación repetitiva de la crudeza del funk negro, alargada por máquinas y no por músicos que improvisan. Nació en clubes europeos de finales de los sesenta que pinchaban funk original, llegó a Estados Unidos y en 1974 era la moda de la Costa Este: aceleró la destrucción de la sesión en directo, de las bandas y de la grabación con alma, y la música negra se volvió más mecánica y menos significativa. El disco quería bailar sin fin sobre un ritmo único; el funk, levantarse y hacer jam («Freak of the Week»: nada de ese «disco sádico» de un solo golpe). Las bandas de funk lo atacaron («The Undisco Kidd», «Anti-Disco» de Mutiny) o se vendieron: James Brown se proclamó «Original Disco Man», los Ohio Players, los Isley y Earth, Wind & Fire («Boogie Wonderland») cayeron. El grito «Disco sucks» metió en el mismo saco a toda la música negra de baile, y muchas bandas de funk murieron por no vender como el disco.

scenes.name: Carreras en solitario: cantautores de finales de los sesenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Los excéntricos de Los Ángeles (David Axelrod, cuyos breakbeats orquestales anticipan el trip-hop; Van Dyke Parks y su música de cámara pop; David Ackles, Kim Fowley, Wild Man Fischer) y los herederos del Greenwich (Laura Nyro, Eric Andersen, David Peel, Angus MacLise y Nico, cuyas letanías fúnebres inventan el rock gótico casi por accidente: Marble Index, Desert Shore). Canadá aporta a Leonard Cohen, Gordon Lightfoot, Joni Mitchell (Blue, Hejira) y Neil Young, que con Dylan y Springsteen forma la gran tríada «moral» de la música americana e inventa la guitarra distorsionada que influirá en el grunge. En Texas, Townes Van Zandt; en Gran Bretaña, Scott Walker, Nick Drake (Pink Moon), Roy Harper, John Martyn, Cat Stevens, Rod Stewart, Eric Burdon y Jack Bruce.

podcast.body: When Rod Stewart was 16 years old, Joe Meek considered hiring a group he was part of, but only on the strict condition that they dismiss Stewart from the band. xref.title: London Show and Drummer's Death
xref.body: In November 1972, Rod Stewart invited the New York Dolls to London to open a show for him. During this trip, drummer Billy Mercier became intoxicated, and after being taken back to an apartment by two groupies, he was dunked in cold water in a bathtub and had coffee poured down his throat, leading to his suffocation and drowning. "But then drummer Billy Mercier got drunk. Two groupies hauled them back to their apartment, dunked them in cold water in the bathtub, and poured coffee down his throat. He suffocated and he drowned."

xref.title: Small Faces Became Faces When Rod Stewart and Ronnie Wood Joined – Both Later Became Rock Royalty
xref.body: When Steve Marriott left the Small Faces in 1969 to form Humble Pie, the rest of the group hired a new guitarist and a new singer. The guitarist was Ronnie Wood, who six years later would replace Mick Taylor in the Rolling Stones. The singer was a gravel-voiced former grave digger named Rod Stewart. The name changed from Small Faces to simply the Faces — because the two tall new members made the "small" descriptor irrelevant. "The new guitarist was Ronnie Wood. Six years later he'd replace Mick Taylor in the Rolling Stones."

xref.body: Despite The New Radicals being known for a single major hit, Greg Alexander successfully leveraged that into a long-term career as a highly in-demand and well-paid mainstream songwriter. He has penned songs for numerous prominent artists, including Santana, Enrique Iglesias, Geri Halliwell, Rod Stewart, Kaiser Chiefs, and The Struts, sometimes using pseudonyms. "Well, that's because he's gone on to write songs for Santana and Enrique Glesias and Jerry Hallwell and Rod Stewart and Kaiser Chiefs and the Struts and many others, sometimes under his own name, sometimes under a pseudonym."

xref.body: Beyond Motown, Bobby Jean Hall has an impressive client list that includes a diverse range of legendary artists.
